claim: Most studies of auditory segregation have used relatively simple signals, in contrast to the complex acoustic environments encountered in everyday life.
source_text: In contrast to the complex acoustic environments we encounter everyday, most studies of auditory segregation have used relatively simple signals.
evidence_reasoning: This statement reflects established knowledge about the state of auditory segregation research and is presented as background context.

claim: Human listeners are remarkably sensitive to the emergence of coherent patterns ('figures') from overlapping 'background' signals in the synthesized stimulus.
source_text: In a series of experiments, we demonstrate that human listeners are remarkably sensitive to the emergence of such figures and can tolerate a variety of spectral and temporal perturbations.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from the series of psychophysical experiments reported in the manuscript (Experiments 1-6).

claim: Human listeners can tolerate a variety of spectral and temporal perturbations when detecting figures from background signals.
source_text: In a series of experiments, we demonstrate that human listeners are remarkably sensitive to the emergence of such figures and can tolerate a variety of spectral and temporal perturbations.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated through experimental manipulations in Experiments 3-6 involving chord duration changes, ramped figures, and noise interruptions.

claim: The observed behavior is consistent with the existence of automatic auditory segregation mechanisms that are highly sensitive to correlations across frequency and time.
source_text: This robust behavior is consistent with the existence of automatic auditory segregation mechanisms that are highly sensitive to correlations across frequency and time.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the experimental results showing robust performance across various conditions, suggesting automatic mechanisms.

claim: The observed behavior cannot be explained purely on the basis of adaptation-based models used to explain the segregation of deterministic narrowband signals.
source_text: The observed behavior cannot be explained purely on the basis of adaptation-based models used to explain the segregation of deterministic narrowband signals.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the comparison of experimental results with predictions from adaptation-based models, particularly noting that figure and background overlap in frequency space.

claim: The results are consistent with the predictions of a model of auditory perceptual organization based on temporal coherence.
source_text: We show that the present results are consistent with the predictions of a model of auditory perceptual organization based on temporal coherence.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the modeling results presented in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1, which show agreement between model predictions and behavioral data.

claim: Temporal coherence plays a role as an organizational principle underlying auditory segregation.
source_text: Our data thus support a role for temporal coherence as an organizational principle underlying auditory segregation.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is drawn from the combined experimental and modeling results showing that temporal coherence accounts for the observed segregation behavior.

claim: The separation of mixtures of sounds into perceptually distinct sound sources is a highly complex task.
source_text: Although we do it effortlessly, the separation of such mixtures of sounds into perceptually distinct sound sources is a highly complex task.
evidence_reasoning: This reflects established understanding in auditory neuroscience about the computational complexity of auditory scene analysis.

claim: The neural bases of auditory object formation and segregation remain to be fully explained.
source_text: In spite of being a topic of intense investigation for several decades, the neural bases of auditory object formation and segregation still remain to be fully explained
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Cherry, 1953; McDermott, 2009; Griffiths et al., 2012) and reflects the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: A sequence of two pure tones alternating in time can 'stream' or segregate into two sources under certain conditions.
source_text: The most commonly used signal for probing auditory perceptual organization is a sequence of two pure tones alternating in time that, under certain conditions, can 'stream' or segregate into two sources
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (van Noorden, 1975; Bregman, 1990) and represents established knowledge about auditory streaming.

claim: For large frequency differences and fast presentation rates in streaming sequences, spatially segregated responses to the two tones are observed in auditory cortex of macaques.
source_text: For large frequency differences and fast presentation rates, which promote two distinct perceptual streams, they observed spatially segregated responses to the two tones.
evidence_reasoning: This refers to findings from Fishman et al. (2001; 2004) as cited in the text.

claim: The pattern of segregated cortical activation has been attributed to basic physiological principles of frequency selectivity, forward masking and neural adaptation.
source_text: This pattern of segregated cortical activation, proposed to underlie the streaming percept, has since been widely replicated (e.g., Bee and Klump, 2004; 2005; Micheyl et al., 2007a; Bidet-Caulet and Bertrand, 2009) and attributed to basic physiological principles of frequency selectivity, forward masking and neural adaptation
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations indicating replicated findings and theoretical interpretations.

claim: Processes contributing to segregation might occur in the auditory nerve rather than be mediated exclusively by the auditory cortex.
source_text: However, similar effects have also been demonstrated in the auditory nerve, suggesting that processes contributing to segregation might occur earlier in the ascending auditory pathway rather than be mediated exclusively by the auditory cortex
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Beauvois and Meddis, 1991; Pressnitzer et al., 2008.

claim: The streaming paradigm uses relatively simple, temporally regular narrowband signals which do not capture the rich spectrotemporal complexity of natural acoustic scenes.
source_text: A major drawback of the streaming paradigm is that it uses relatively simple, temporally regular narrowband signals which do not capture the rich spectrotemporal complexity of natural acoustic scenes.
evidence_reasoning: This is a critical assessment of the streaming paradigm based on comparison with natural acoustic environments.

claim: Target detection in informational masking experiments is critically dependent on the width of the spectral protection region and the density of the maskers.
source_text: Results demonstrate that target detection is critically dependent on the width of the spectral protection region, and the 'density' of the maskers
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Micheyl et al., 2007b; Gutschalk et al., 2008; Elhilali et al., 2009b.

claim: Sounds in everyday life are often broadband with multiple frequency components that are temporally correlated and overlap with other signals in the environment.
source_text: In contrast, the sounds we are required to segregate in everyday life are distinct from the narrowband targets used in streaming and IM paradigms; they are often broadband with multiple frequency components that are temporally correlated and overlap with other signals in the environment
evidence_reasoning: This reflects knowledge about natural sounds, supported by citation to McDermott and Simoncelli, 2011.

claim: When two tones in a streaming signal are presented synchronously, listeners perceive the sequence as one stream irrespective of the frequency separation between the two tones.
source_text: Recently, Elhilali et al. (2009a) demonstrated that when the two tones in a streaming signal are presented synchronously, listeners perceive the sequence as one stream irrespective of the frequency separation between the two tones
evidence_reasoning: This refers to specific findings from Elhilali et al. (2009a).

claim: Temporal coherence between different elements in the scene is essential for segregation such that temporally incoherent patterns tend to result in a segregated percept while temporal coherence promotes integration.
source_text: Instead, the authors argued that in addition to separation in feature space, temporal coherence between different elements in the scene is essential for segregation such that temporally incoherent patterns tend to result in a segregated percept while temporal coherence promotes integration
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Shamma et al., 2011; Fishman and Steinschneider, 2010b; Micheyl et al., 2013a,b.

claim: In Experiment 1, listeners showed a clear effect of increasing coherence and duration on figure detection performance.
source_text: The results (Figure 2A) show a clear effect of increasing coherence and duration.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by the experimental data presented in Figure 2A.

claim: Listeners achieved mean hit rates of 93 ± 2% for the most salient coherence/duration combination in Experiment 1.
source_text: Hit rates (not shown) mirror d′ with listeners achieving mean hit rates of 93 ± 2% for the most salient coherence/duration combination.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of measured behavioral data from Experiment 1.

claim: The patterns in the SFG stimulus were very brief (longest figure duration was 7 chords or 350 ms), yet very high levels of performance were observed without extensive practice.
source_text: It is notable that the patterns were very brief (longest figure duration was 7 chords or 350 ms), yet very high levels of performance were observed (and without extensive practice).
evidence_reasoning: This observation is based on the experimental design and measured performance data.

claim: The high performance with brief patterns and minimal training is consistent with the idea that the SFG task taps low-level, finely tuned segregation mechanisms.
source_text: This is consistent with the idea that this task based on the SFG stimulus taps low-level, finely tuned segregation mechanisms.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation of high performance with minimal training.

claim: A global power increase per se associated with the emergence of the figure can be discounted as a potential cue for figure detection.
source_text: Since 'figure-absent' and 'figure-present' signals were controlled for overall number of components (see 'Materials and methods'), a global power increase per se associated with the emergence of the figure, can be discounted as a potential cue.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the experimental design where figure-absent and figure-present signals were controlled for number of components.

claim: In Experiment 2, listeners could identify the 'odd' signal containing a different figure from two signals with identical figures.
source_text: Results (Figure 2B) show that listeners were able to perform this task well above chance
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by the behavioral data from Experiment 2 shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The figure detection involves a specific figure-ground decomposition where figure components are grouped together as a detectable 'perceptual object' distinct from the background components.
source_text: To address this issue, we created stimulus triplets with different background patterns in which each stimulus contained a figure but where figure components were identical in two out of the three signals. Listeners were required to identify the 'odd' signal that contained a different figure from the other two signals with identical figures in this AXB psychophysical paradigm
evidence_reasoning: The ability of listeners to perform the AXB task (Experiment 2) demonstrates that they perceive the figure as a distinct object, not just detecting low-level changes.

claim: It is difficult to account for listeners' performance in experiments 1 and 2 based on standard, adaptation-based models proposed in the context of the streaming paradigm.
source_text: It is difficult to account for listeners' performance in experiments 1 and 2 based on the standard, adaptation-based models proposed in the context of the streaming paradigm
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the comparison of the experimental results with the predictions of adaptation-based models.

claim: The figure and background in the SFG stimuli overlap in frequency space, challenging segregation based on activation of spatially distinct neuronal populations in A1.
source_text: The figure and background in the SFG stimuli overlap in frequency space, thus challenging segregation based on activation of spatially distinct neuronal populations in A1.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the stimulus design where figure and background components are drawn from the same frequency pool.

claim: Performance strongly depends on the number of simultaneously repeating frequency components, suggesting a mechanism that can integrate across widely spaced frequency channels.
source_text: Furthermore, the data clearly indicate that performance strongly depends on the number of simultaneously repeating frequency components, suggesting a mechanism that is able to integrate across widely spaced frequency channels
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the experimental data showing performance variation with coherence (number of repeating components).

claim: The psychophysical data are consistent with a model of auditory object formation based on analysis of temporal coherence.
source_text: Instead, the psychophysical data are consistent with a recently proposed model of auditory object formation based on analysis of temporal coherence
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the comparison of behavioral data with model predictions shown in Figure 3 and supplements.

claim: The temporal coherence model proposes that a perceptual 'stream' emerges when a group of frequency channels are coherently activated against the backdrop of other uncorrelated channels.
source_text: The temporal coherence model is based on the idea that a perceptual 'stream' emerges when a group of (frequency) channels are coherently activated against the backdrop of other uncorrelated channels
evidence_reasoning: This describes the theoretical basis of the temporal coherence model as proposed by Shamma and Micheyl, 2010.

claim: The temporal coherence model incorporates a spectrotemporal analysis postulated to take place in the auditory cortex.
source_text: The computations incorporated a spectrotemporal analysis postulated to take place in the auditory cortex
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the model framework described in cited works (Chi et al., 2005).

claim: In Experiment 3, listeners achieved hit rates of 92 ± 3% for the highest coherence/duration combination with 25 ms chords.
source_text: Listeners achieved hit rates of 92 ± 3% for the highest coherence/duration combination used.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of measured behavioral data from Experiment 3.

claim: Performance in figure detection largely depends on the number of repeating chords irrespective of the time scale.
source_text: An ANOVA with coherence and duration as within-subject factors and experimental condition (50 ms vs 25 ms chords) as a between-subject factor revealed no significant effect of condition (F1,15 = 2; p=0.174), suggesting that performance largely depends on the number of repeating chords irrespective of the time scale.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical analysis comparing Experiments 1 and 3.

claim: In Experiment 4, listeners exhibited above-chance performance even for the steeper frequency ramp (ramp size = 5).
source_text: Performance was significantly worse for the ramp = 5 vs ramp = 2 condition (F1,18 = 21, p<0.001), but, remarkably, listeners exhibited above-chance performance even for the steeper slope.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by the behavioral data from Experiment 4b.

claim: The segregation mechanisms are more susceptible to spectral than temporal perturbations.
source_text: This suggests that the segregation mechanisms in question are more susceptible to spectral than temporal perturbations (as in experiments 3, and 6 below) but can still integrate over dynamically changing, rather than fixed, figure components.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from comparing performance across experiments with different types of perturbations.

claim: In Experiment 5, the 'background-only' chords which preceded the figure did not affect performance.
source_text: To evaluate behavior with respect to experiment 1, an ANOVA with coherence and duration as within-subject factors and experimental condition (with background vs no background) as a between-subject factor was used which yielded no significant effect of condition: F1,16 = 0.033; p=0.859, suggesting that the 'background-only' chords which preceded the figure did not affect performance.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical comparison between Experiments 1 and 5.

claim: Segregation is not mediated by adaptation to the ongoing background statistics and detection of the figure as a deviation from this established pattern.
source_text: From first principles, segregation could be considered to be mediated by adaptation to the ongoing background statistics and detection of the figure as a deviation from this established pattern. In order to test this hypothesis, in experiment 5, we removed the 'background' context which preceded the occurrence of the figure
evidence_reasoning: The lack of performance difference in Experiment 5 (without background context) compared to Experiment 1 suggests adaptation to background is not necessary.

claim: In Experiment 6a, interleaving noise bursts between successive chords does not affect figure detection performance.
source_text: An ANOVA with coherence and duration as within-subject factors and experimental condition (50 ms repeating chords vs 50 ms chords alternating with white noise) as a between-subject factor revealed no significant effect of condition (F1,17 = 0.004; p=0.953). Interleaving the noise bursts between successive chords does not therefore affect performance.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical comparison between Experiments 1 and 6a.

claim: Listeners can integrate coherent patterns over time windows as long as 3 seconds.
source_text: This remarkable ability of listeners to integrate coherent patterns over 3 s long (in the case of 500 ms noise bursts) suggests that the underlying higher-order mechanisms are very robust over such long time windows.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the results from Experiment 6b showing above-chance performance with 500 ms noise interruptions.

claim: In Experiment 6b, listeners showed supra-threshold performance (d′ = 1.00 ± 0.30) for a noise duration of 500 ms.
source_text: Results (Figure 4E) indicate robust performance for all durations of noise up to 300 ms and surprisingly, supra-threshold performance (d′ = 1.00 ± 0.30; significantly different from 0: p=0.01; t = 3.29) for a noise duration of 500 ms.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of measured behavioral data from Experiment 6b with statistical significance testing.

claim: Temporal windows of integration as long as 500 ms have rarely been reported in the context of auditory object formation in complex scenes.
source_text: Temporal windows of integration, as long as 500 ms, have rarely been reported in the context of auditory object formation in complex scenes such as those examined here.
evidence_reasoning: This reflects knowledge about the existing literature on temporal integration in auditory object formation.

claim: The long temporal windows implicate cortical mechanisms at or beyond primary auditory cortex.
source_text: The long temporal windows here implicate cortical mechanisms at or beyond primary auditory cortex (see e.g., Overath et al., 2008 demonstrating a range of 'cortical windows' between 20 ms and 300 ms).
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the temporal integration results and supported by citation to Overath et al., 2008.

claim: Figures can be detected as objects that can be distinguished, consistent with a high-level mechanism for object detection as opposed to simple detection of frequency or modulation cues.
source_text: We show that such figures can be detected as objects that can be distinguished, consistent with a high-level mechanism for object detection as opposed to the simple detection of frequency or modulation cues (experiment 2).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the results of Experiment 2 (AXB task) showing figure identification.

claim: The segregation mechanism scales in time, in that detection depends on the number of components over time rather than their absolute duration.
source_text: The mechanism scales in time, in that detection depends on the number of components over time rather than their absolute duration (experiment 3)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the comparison between Experiments 1 and 3 showing no effect of chord duration.

claim: The segregation mechanism can still operate if the object is defined by slowly changing frequency trajectories rather than a fixed set of frequencies.
source_text: and can still operate if the object is defined by slowly changing frequency trajectories rather than a fixed set of frequencies (experiment 4).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the results of Experiment 4 showing above-chance performance with ramped figures.

claim: The segregation mechanism is robust to interruption of the figure by interleaved noise.
source_text: It is robust to interruption of the figure by interleaved noise (experiment 5)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the results of Experiment 6a showing no performance decrement with noise interruptions.

claim: The segregation mechanism can operate over a remarkably long timescale.
source_text: and can operate over a remarkably long timescale (experiment 6).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the results of Experiment 6b showing performance with 500 ms noise interruptions.

claim: Modeling based on temporal coherence demonstrated a similar profile to the behavioral results.
source_text: Modeling based on temporal coherence demonstrated a similar profile to the behavioral results
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the modeling results shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: This work constitutes the first demonstration of the compatibility of the temporal coherence model with segregation in complex acoustic scenes.
source_text: and constitutes the first demonstration of the compatibility of the temporal coherence model with segregation in complex acoustic scenes.
evidence_reasoning: This is a claim about the novelty of the work based on the modeling and experimental results.

claim: Segregation is determined not only based on separation in feature-space but rather by the temporal relationship between different elements in the scene.
source_text: The temporal coherence model proposes that segregation is determined not only based on separation in feature-space but rather by the temporal relationship between different elements in the scene
evidence_reasoning: This describes the theoretical framework of the temporal coherence model as proposed by Shamma et al., 2011.

claim: Temporally coherent elements are grouped together, while temporally incoherent channels with independent fluctuation profiles are perceived as belonging to separate sources.
source_text: such that temporally coherent elements are grouped together, while temporally incoherent channels with independent fluctuation profiles are perceived as belonging to separate sources
evidence_reasoning: This is part of the theoretical framework of the temporal coherence model cited from Shamma et al., 2011.

claim: The temporal coherence model incorporates a feature analysis stage that performs multidimensional feature analysis by distinct populations of neurons in the auditory cortex.
source_text: Specifically, the model incorporates two stages: firstly, a feature analysis stage that performs multidimensional feature analysis by distinct populations of neurons in the auditory cortex that are tuned to a range of temporal modulation rates and spectral resolution scales.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the computational architecture of the temporal coherence model based on cited work.

claim: A pair of synchronous repeating tones produces the same coherent pattern of modeled central activity as a single stream irrespective of the frequency separation between them.
source_text: they showed that a pair of synchronous repeating tones produces the same coherent pattern of modeled central activity as a single stream irrespective of the frequency separation between them
evidence_reasoning: This refers to findings from Elhilali et al. (2009a) as cited in the text.

claim: Synchronous and alternating cortical responses in ferret auditory cortex were equally segregated despite their perceptual differences.
source_text: This was substantiated by direct neurophysiological recordings from ferret auditory cortex which showed that synchronous and alternating cortical responses were equally segregated despite their perceptual differences
evidence_reasoning: This refers to neurophysiological findings cited from Shamma and Micheyl, 2010; Pressnitzer et al., 2011; Shamma et al., 2011, 2013.

claim: Temporal coherence is modulated as a function of the coherence and the duration of the figure in a manner similar to the modulation of figure detection performance.
source_text: In the case of the more complex SFG stimuli, the modeling results suggest that temporal coherence is modulated as a function of the coherence and the duration of the figure in a manner similar to the modulation of figure detection performance.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the modeling results showing correspondence between model output and behavioral performance.

claim: Temporal coherence may serve as a correlate of stimulus salience by which the brain picks out the most important sounds in busy auditory scenes.
source_text: The data suggest temporal coherence as a correlate of stimulus salience by which the brain picks out the most important sounds in busy auditory scenes
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the correspondence between temporal coherence modeling and behavioral performance.

claim: Binding across distributed feature channels could be achieved without significant changes in ensemble activity.
source_text: a process that may not be computed by dedicated structures but could be achieved by binding across distributed feature channels without significant changes in ensemble activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about the neural implementation of temporal coherence.

claim: It is not known how temporal coherence may be computed and which brain areas perform these computations.
source_text: It is still not known how temporal coherence may be computed and which brain areas perform these computations.
evidence_reasoning: This reflects the current state of knowledge about the neural implementation of temporal coherence.

claim: Temporal coherence may be implemented by neurons that show strong sensitivity to temporal coherence across distant frequency channels, or by neurons that act as multiplexers.
source_text: Temporal coherence may be implemented by neurons that show strong sensitivity to temporal coherence across distant frequency channels, or by neurons that act as multiplexers and are more selective to particular combinations of inputs
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about possible neural mechanisms, supported by citations to Elhilali et al., 2009a; Shamma et al., 2011.

claim: Elhilali et al. were unable to demonstrate neurons sensitive to temporal coherence in the primary auditory cortex of passively listening ferrets.
source_text: Elhilali et al. (2009a) sought such cells in the primary auditory cortex of the ferret but were unable to demonstrate any in passively listening animals
evidence_reasoning: This refers to findings from Elhilali et al. (2009a) as cited in the text.

claim: There is preliminary evidence for neurons sensitive to temporal coherence in behaving ferrets.
source_text: but have preliminary evidence in behaving ferrets (Shamma et al., 2013).
evidence_reasoning: This refers to preliminary findings cited from Shamma et al., 2013.

claim: No evidence of modulation of BOLD signal in A1 as a function of figure emergence was found in a passive listening paradigm.
source_text: Although previous brain imaging studies have identified activity in A1 that was correlated with the streaming percept (e.g., Gutschalk et al., 2005; Snyder et al., 2006; Wilson et al., 2007), we found no evidence of modulation of BOLD signal in A1 as a function of figure emergence in a passive listening paradigm (Teki et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This refers to findings from the authors' previous fMRI study (Teki et al., 2011).

claim: Activity in the intraparietal sulcus (IPS) was strongly modulated by the salience of the figure.
source_text: However, we found activity in the intraparietal sulcus (IPS) to be strongly modulated by the salience of the figure, similar to the modulation of temporal coherence observed here.
evidence_reasoning: This refers to findings from the authors' previous fMRI study (Teki et al., 2011).

claim: The IPS activation likely reflects bottom-up stimulus-driven processing of figures.
source_text: The IPS activation likely reflect bottom-up stimulus-driven processing of figures
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the IPS activation pattern and supported by reference to the authors' previous work.

claim: Areas outside the conventional auditory system, such as the parietal cortex, may have a role in auditory segregation.
source_text: and is consistent with accumulating literature which suggests that areas outside the conventional auditory system, such as the parietal cortex may have a role in auditory segregation
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Cusack, 2005; Dykstra et al., 2011.

claim: The parietal cortex receives auditory input from the temporoparietal cortex.
source_text: In this regard, the parietal cortex is in an ideal position to integrate both bottom-up auditory input as it receives auditory input from the temporoparietal cortex
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to anatomical studies (Pandya and Kuypers, 1969; Divac et al., 1977; Hyvärinen, 1982; Cohen, 2009).

claim: The parietal cortex receives top-down attentional input from the prefrontal cortex.
source_text: as well as top-down attentional input from the prefrontal cortex
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to anatomical studies (Andersen et al., 1985; Barbas and Mesulam, 1981; Petrides and Pandya, 1984; Stanton et al., 1995).

claim: IPS is associated with both bottom-up and top-down attention and is a key structure implicated in saliency map models of visual search.
source_text: IPS is associated with both bottom-up and top-down attention and is a key structure implicated in saliency map models of visual search
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Koch and Ullman, 1985; Itti and Koch, 2001; Walther and Koch, 2007.

claim: IPS has been implicated in mediating object representations, binding of sensory features within and across different modalities, as well as attentional selection.
source_text: IPS (and its monkey homologue) has been implicated in mediating object representations, binding of sensory features within and across different modalities, as well as attentional selection.
evidence_reasoning: This reflects established knowledge about the functional roles of IPS based on the literature.

claim: IPS may represent a neural correlate of the figure percept where the representation depends on the salience of auditory figures.
source_text: We hypothesize that IPS may represent a neural correlate of the figure percept where the representation will depend on the salience of auditory figures.
evidence_reasoning: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their fMRI findings and the modeling results.

claim: The perceptual representation in IPS depends on the computation of temporal coherence across multiple frequencies that are initially represented in the auditory cortex.
source_text: In our model, this perceptual representation depends on the computation of temporal coherence across multiple frequencies that are initially represented in the auditory cortex.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about the computational relationship between auditory cortex and IPS.

claim: The SFG stimulus consists of a sequence of random chords where a random number of tones are repeated across consecutive chords, resulting in the percept of a 'figure' that pops out of the random tonal background.
source_text: In half of these stimuli, a random number of tones are repeated across a certain number of consecutive chords (e.g., in Figure 1, four components marked by arrows are repeated across 6 chords) which results in the percept of a 'figure' that readily pops out of the random tonal background.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the stimulus design and the perceptual effect it produces.

claim: To eliminate correlation between the number of figure and background components, the figure was realized by adding additional, repeating components to the random background.
source_text: To eliminate correlation between the number of figure and background components, the figure was realized by first generating the random background and then adding additional, repeating components to the relevant chords.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the methodological approach to control for potential confounds in the stimulus design.

claim: In figure-absent stimuli, additional tonal components were added that changed from chord to chord and did not form a coherent figure.
source_text: But these additional components changed from chord to chord and did not form a coherent figure.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the control condition design to match the number of components between figure-present and figure-absent stimuli.

claim: All participants tested reported normal hearing and had no history of audiological or neurological disorders.
source_text: All participants tested in this set of experiments reported normal hearing and had no history of audiological or neurological disorders.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the participant inclusion criteria for the experiments.

claim: Experimental procedures were approved by the research ethics committee of University College London.
source_text: Experimental procedures were approved by the research ethics committee of University College London (Project ID number: 1490/002), and written informed consent was obtained from each participant.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the ethical approval and consent procedures for the study.
